summary: 14-day Nightscout/AAPS review with good CGM coverage shows TIR 86.0% but TBR 5.1% with recurrent 41-42 mg/dL lows clustered locally at 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00. Afternoon TAR is high while carb entries are zero, so UAM/SMB and Dynamic ISF are the observed meal pathway. The only supported profile review is raising the overnight 90 mg/dL target to 100 mg/dL; basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and AAPS groups stay unchanged until that single change is observed.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM is usable for later inference. Profile object is complete and declared historically applicable. Carb telemetry is absent, so CR and meal-parameter inference is limited rather than blocked for safety and basal description.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid 5-minute entries, 98.7% coverage, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, 0 invalid or duplicate entries. treatments 2315, insulin entries 655, total insulin 275.95 U, carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0. profile_context.historical_applicability is yes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal composition, activity log, or e-carb records. Mid-period confounders include the 13 Aug profile switch note, site and sensor changes, 19 Aug occlusion/pump error, and GLP-1 1.25 mg notes.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall control is strong, but TBR above a 4% guardrail is the binding constraint and must limit every later change. Severe lows and evening/night TBR clusters outweigh the afternoon highs as the first safety problem.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7, CV 32.6%, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%. Extremes include 41-45 mg/dL on 13-14 Aug evenings and 42 mg/dL on 21 Aug 06:19. Local-hour TBR: 01:00 18.5%, 19:00 15.3%, 00:00 11.4%, 23:00/02:00/03:00 about 10%. Local TAR peaks 14:00-17:00, highest 16:00 at 32.1%.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality coverage is sufficient for hypo and hyper counts.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No hypo-treatment, rescue-carb, or exercise annotations. Day-level TBR spikes on 11, 14, and 18 Aug cannot be attributed to a single cause without those labels.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight means sit near the 90 mg/dL target while TBR is high through 03:00, so raising overnight basal is not supported. 04:00-08:00 looks stable. Daytime rises align with unlogged meal timing and later insulin action more than with a proven basal defect. Scheduled basal is often overridden by zero temps when minGuardBG is low.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local averages: 00:00 93.3, 01:00 90.6, 04:00-07:00 about 99-106 with TIR 95-99%. Afternoon 14:00-16:00 averages 148-163 then 18:00-19:00 TBR 7.7% and 15.3% with minima 41-42. Basal segments 0.5-0.8 U/h, night target 90, day target 100 from 08:00.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview TBR forbids strengthening overnight insulin first. data_quality has no fasting or activity labels.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True fasting windows cannot be isolated. Profile switch, GLP-1 notes, and the 19 Aug occlusion split the 14 days, so overnight basal versus residual IOB remains unresolved.

analysis_steps.findings: CR segments exist but are unused because no carbs were logged. Flat ISF 56 is not the delivered correction factor while Dynamic ISF is on. DIA 10 h is long and can leave evening IOB active overnight, but it cannot be isolated from SMB/UAM.
analysis_steps.evidence: CR 13/11.1/13.2/10.5/12.6 g/U, ISF 56 mg/dL/U, DIA 10 h. All 24 therapy windows are Correction Bolus. Loop variable_sens about 28-124. Small listed corrections cannot explain large 120-minute drops such as 234 to 56 mg/dL after 0.2 U.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets and safety_overview. Do not retune CR or ISF to fix patterns still explained by missing meals, UAM, or target.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No paired carb, bolus, and absorption records. Insulin dilution and free_peak_oref peak are not independently verified. Correction windows are confounded by SMB, UAM, and unlogged meals.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are the live meal and correction engine. Activation flags are consistent with zero COB. Observed SMB size sometimes follows high temp basal, not profile basal times 15-20 minutes. Always-on UAM through the afternoon is a leading explanation for evening IOB and later TBR.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled and uam_enabled true, smb_always_enabled true, COB 0 in representative reasons. Statuses show 0.3-0.4 U SMBs and one 1.6 U UAM High Boost on 19 Aug after occlusion. Interval is 3 minutes; remaining zero-temp time is not the interval.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview TBR; basal_targets competing night-basal hypothesis; unused CR.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal timestamps to score UAM true or false positives. Occlusion, site changes, and GLP-1 notes confound aggressive SMB versus catch-up dosing.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off and target auto-adjust is off. Dynamic ISF at 70% dominates effective ISF. Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h are loose versus about 20 U/day but were not the binding cap in the sample. Carb-absorption settings are idle.
analysis_steps.evidence: sensitivity_ratio is often 1 and sometimes 0.79-0.98; 1 is a neutral adjustment, not proof Autosens is on. Enacted temps cap near maxSafeBasal about 4 U/h. Peak representative IOB 5.935 U at BG 245.7. min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 with COB 0.
analysis_steps.dependencies: SMB/UAM coupling; ISF 56 must not be changed with DynISF in the same step.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The share of variable_sens near 28 that comes from DynISF versus UAM boost versus high IOB cannot be quantified. Peak time for free_peak_oref is not in the inventory.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal strategy is empty. Observed execution is unannounced meals plus corrections and UAM/SMB. No prebolus minutes or immediate bolus percent exist to reproduce. Afternoon highs then evening lows are not evidence for a larger meal bolus.
analysis_steps.evidence: analysis_context.meal_strategies is []. strategy_stable_for_period is null. carb_treatment_entries empty. Representative treatments are temp basal and correction bolus only.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused; SMB always on; DIA 10 h; night target 90; TBR constraint.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: prebolus_minutes and immediate_bolus_percent are null in the declaration, and Nightscout has no meal-labeled boluses to infer them.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are not declared and not present in telemetry. Idle absorption settings cannot be judged. E-carbs are not an extended pump bolus and no duration should be inferred.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min null, total_carbs_g 0. Glucose action is only the 14:00-17:00 peak and 18:00-19:00 plus overnight TBR clusters.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared or logged e-carb amount, start offset, or duration. Regular carb entries are also absent, so absorption time cannot be scored.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked explanation for TBR is residual afternoon or evening UAM/SMB IOB plus DIA 10 h plus overnight target 90, with Dynamic ISF making effective ISF stronger than 56. Overnight basal too low is unlikely because night means already sit near 90 while TBR is high. Afternoon TAR is not a 10:00-16:00 basal defect while meals are unlogged. The only profile change that reduces insulin pressure without requiring those explanations to be fully separated is raising overnight target 90 to 100 mg/dL. Keep basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and all six AAPS groups. Observe that single target change before any SMB, DynISF, or basal review.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local TBR clusters under target 90; existing daytime target already 100; automation reasons show COB 0, frequent zero temps, and variable_sens well below 56; no carb entries to support CR or e-carb changes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All prior stages. Do not combine the target review with basal, ISF, DynISF, or SMB delivery changes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meal timing and leftover-IOB versus target-driven lows remain unseparated until after a single overnight-target observation and some carb or meal marks.

strengths: CGM coverage 98.7% with regular 5-minute cadence and no invalid entries.
Overall TIR 86.0% and CV 32.6% over 14 days.
Local 04:00-08:00 windows show high TIR and low TBR.
Authoritative AAPS profile is complete, historically marked applicable, and basal total 16.2 U/day matches the dilute-basal note.
Loop already sets zero temporary basal when predicted guard glucose is low.
issues: TBR 5.1% with recurrent severe lows to 41-42 mg/dL.
Night TBR cluster at local 23:00-03:00 under target 90 mg/dL.
Afternoon TAR then 18:00-19:00 crash pattern with unlogged meals.
Zero carb entries so CR and e-carb settings are unused and UAM/SMB carry meal dosing.
Dynamic ISF produces much stronger effective ISF than the flat 56 mg/dL/U segment.
Period confounders include GLP-1 notes, site/sensor changes, and a 19 Aug occlusion.

recommendations.title: Review raising overnight target from 90 to 100 mg/dL
recommendations.description: Local TBR is concentrated under the 90 mg/dL overnight target while night means are already near that target. Raising only 23:00 and 00:00 to the existing daytime 100 mg/dL value reduces overnight insulin pressure whether lows are residual UAM/SMB IOB or target-driven, without strengthening basal.

recommendations.title: Defer basal, ISF, SMB, and DynISF reviews
recommendations.description: Afternoon highs and evening lows have several coupled explanations. Changing basal, ISF 56, DynISF 70%, or SMB strength in the same step as the overnight target would prevent attribution and can stack insulin.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Review changing overnight target segments at 23:00 and 00:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL and keep every other profile segment unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Night TBR is the binding pattern. Means at 00:00-03:00 already sit near 90 mg/dL, so more overnight basal is not supported. 100 mg/dL is already the 08:00 target, so the candidate is an existing profile value rather than a new invented target. Residual UAM/SMB IOB remains an alternate cause, which is why confidence is medium and no second profile change is paired with this review.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After this single target review only, compare 7 nights of local 23:00-03:00 TBR and whether lows occur with near-zero IOB versus leftover afternoon IOB.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local 00:00-03:00 TBR is high while average glucose is already near 90 mg/dL. Uncertainty: residual IOB versus basal cannot be fully split. Dependencies: safety TBR and pending overnight target review; do not raise this basal.
Evidence: local 05:00-06:00 TIR 95.2% and TBR 4.8% with mean 104.2. Uncertainty: one 21 Aug 06:19 value of 42 mg/dL. Dependencies: do not change adjacent night segments together.
Evidence: local 06:00-08:00 TIR 97.5-98.7% with low TBR. Uncertainty: later 08:00-10:00 rise is meal-timed. Dependencies: unused breakfast carbs; withhold as a dawn-basal increase.

Evidence: 10:00 TAR 20.2% sits in a likely meal window with COB 0. Uncertainty: UAM versus basal under-delivery. Dependencies: meal logging and SMB/UAM; do not raise daytime basal to chase unlogged peaks.

Evidence: 16:00 is the TAR peak and also precedes the 18:00-19:00 crash, so more 16:00 insulin can worsen TBR. Uncertainty: lowest scheduled basal versus stacked UAM. Dependencies: evening hypo cluster and DIA 10 h.
Evidence: local 18:00 TBR 7.7% and minima 42 mg/dL. Uncertainty: exercise, GLP-1, or IOB carryover. Dependencies: binding TBR; do not increase this segment.
Evidence: local 19:00 TBR 15.3% and minima 41 mg/dL. Uncertainty: whether the 0.7 step-up adds to stacked IOB. Dependencies: target and UAM review first; no increase.
Evidence: carb_entries 0 so this CR is unused. Uncertainty: no meal-linked responses. Dependencies: carb logging before any CR review.
Evidence: no carb treatments in this or any segment. Uncertainty: cannot test 11.1 versus neighboring ratios. Dependencies: empty declared meal strategy and unused wizard.
Evidence: late-morning rise occurs with COB 0 and UAM/SMB, not a logged breakfast bolus. Uncertainty: meal size unknown. Dependencies: do not tighten CR while TBR is binding.

Evidence: this is the tightest CR and coincides with the worst TAR-to-TBR swing, but no carbs were entered. Uncertainty: unused setting versus real afternoon meals. Dependencies: UAM/SMB already dosing; tightening CR is unsupported.
Evidence: evening TBR cluster with zero carb entries. Uncertainty: dinner composition unknown. Dependencies: overnight target review and residual IOB.

Evidence: Dynamic ISF 70% produces variable_sens far from 56, and correction windows are confounded by SMB/UAM. Uncertainty: how much of effective ISF is DynISF versus UAM boost. Dependencies: do not change ISF in the same step as DynISF or target.

Evidence: local 00:00-03:00 TBR 10-18.5% with averages 90-105 already near 90. Uncertainty: leftover IOB may still cause lows after a higher target. Dependencies: change together with 23:00 only; keep 08:00 at 100; do not change basal or SMB at the same time.

Evidence: daytime target 100 is not the overnight TBR window and is the candidate overnight value. Uncertainty: morning 08:00-10:00 TAR is more meal than target. Dependencies: overnight target change uses this existing value.
Evidence: local 23:00 TBR 10.1% begins the overnight 90 mg/dL window. Uncertainty: evening IOB from afternoon UAM. Dependencies: pair only with 00:00 target; withhold basal and automation changes.

Evidence: long DIA is compatible with delayed evening and night lows but is conservative. Uncertainty: free_peak_oref peak not independently verified. Dependencies: shortening DIA while TBR is high would undercount IOB; keep.

Evidence: with carb_entries 0, UAM is the meal detector and is not double-counting COB. Uncertainty: UAM false positives cannot be scored without meal marks. Dependencies: profile target review first; disabling UAM and changing target together is unsupported.

Evidence: always-on SMB makes COB-gated flags non-operative, not inconsistent; high-TT SMB off matches several 135 mg/dL temporary targets. Uncertainty: always-on SMB likely contributes to afternoon stacking. Dependencies: do not retune activation with delivery or DynISF in the same step.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: 3 minute interval is the configured cadence; some large SMBs scaled with high temp basal after occlusion, not with 15-20 minutes times 0.5-0.8 U/h. Uncertainty: delivery versus DynISF versus UAM boost. Dependencies: keep until overnight target effect is observed.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: about 19.7 U/day total insulin; peak sampled IOB 5.935 U; enacted temps already cap near 4 U/h. Uncertainty: 25 U would not stop further stacking if a larger event occurred. Dependencies: limits are hygiene, not the TBR cause; changing them with target is unnecessary.

Evidence: Autosens-off flags match each other; DynISF explains variable_sens 28-124; sensitivity_ratio 1 is neutral, not disabled Autosens. Uncertainty: GLP-1 may change sensitivity outside Autosens. Dependencies: do not change DynISF with ISF 56 or SMB delivery.
Evidence: absorption model is idle with COB 0 and no e-carbs. Uncertainty: cannot judge 8 mg/dL per 5 min or 7 h without logged carbs. Dependencies: meal logging; not a UAM duplicate-count issue.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the observed unannounced-meal pattern: no declared prebolus, no immediate bolus percent, no e-carbs, and UAM/SMB as the meal engine. Do not add CR-based meal boluses or e-carb schedules on top of always-on SMB until carbs are logged.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: User-declared analysis_context has an empty meal_strategies list and null stability flag. Telemetry shows zero carb and e-carb entries, while glucose still has a late-morning wave and a larger afternoon wave followed by evening TBR.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Several days of carb entries with time and grams at the late-morning wave versus the 14:00-16:00 wave.

exceptions.suggestion: Leave UAM/SMB to catch this smaller wave; no prebolus or percent can be added from declared or logged data.
exceptions.rationale: TAR rises then settles with little follow-on TBR compared with the afternoon.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon peak then evening crash about 14:00-19:00
exceptions.suggestion: Do not add meal insulin, tighter 16:00 CR, or e-carbs for this wave while evening TBR is binding.
exceptions.rationale: Extra coverage would stack on SMB/UAM, DynISF, and DIA 10 h that already precede 41-42 mg/dL lows.

implementation_steps: Independently review CGM, IOB, and temporary-target history for local 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00 before any setting edit.
Discuss only the overnight target candidate: 23:00 and 00:00 from 90 to 100 mg/dL. Leave the 08:00 target at 100 mg/dL.
If that review is applied, change those two target segments only, then monitor glucose closely for at least 7 nights.
Do not change basal, CR, ISF, DIA, SMB, UAM, or DynISF in the same step.
After the observation window, compare whether remaining lows occur with near-zero IOB or leftover afternoon IOB before considering any automation review.
If meals continue unlogged, add time-and-gram carb entries before any CR or e-carb discussion.
education: A night mean near target with high TBR is not evidence that overnight basal is too low.
UAM can dose for unlogged meals without creating COB, so COB 0 does not mean no meal insulin was given.
Dynamic ISF can make the working ISF much stronger than the flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U.
E-carbs are a carb-absorption announcement, not a pump extended bolus, and cannot be inferred from an empty average duration.
sensitivity_ratio 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not a sign that Autosens is turned off or on.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and is not medical advice.
The user must independently verify every proposed change with their care team, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TBR 5.1% and recurrent 41-42 mg/dL values are the binding safety constraint; do not strengthen insulin to treat afternoon TAR first.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not change AAPS automatically.
Occlusion, site changes, sensor changes, and GLP-1 notes in this period can mimic profile or automation faults.
